# Implementation Plan: Drift Sync Pipeline (2026-11-01)

## Goal

Make re-running a plan after a local edit refresh exactly the touched task's mirror,
never the whole file, and keep the plan file the single source of truth.

## Architecture

One parser, one extent map, one surgical renderer. Plan files stay plain Markdown;
mirrors carry a visible reference prefix and nothing else.

## Tech Stack

TypeScript, Node 20, zero runtime dependencies.

## Spec reference

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-drift-sync.md — approved 2026-10-30, no open questions.

## Global Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies.
- Parse → render → parse must reproduce every fixture byte-for-byte apart from the prefix.

## Review Focus

Extent boundaries around fenced code blocks; drift detection granularity per task body.

### Task 1: SyncJournalWriter

Own the append-only journal that records each mirror write.

Files:

- src/sync/journal.ts
- tests/unit/sync-journal.test.ts

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing journal round-trip test**
- [ ] **Step 2: Implement the append-only writer with fsync**
- [ ] **Step 3: Wire the journal into the apply lane and re-run the suite**

Run:

```sh
npm run compile:tests && node scripts/run-tests.mjs --tier unit
```

### Task 2: DriftDetector

Hash each task body span and report only the spans that changed.

Files:

- src/sync/drift.ts
- tests/unit/sync-drift.test.ts

- [ ] **Step 4: Add the change-span table test**
- [ ] **Step 5: Implement per-span hashing against the previous manifest**

The detector must ignore the visible reference prefix when comparing bodies.

### Task 3: MirrorRenderer

Render one issue description verbatim from its task body span.

Files:

- src/sync/render.ts
- tests/unit/sync-render.test.ts

- [ ] **Step 6: Pin the byte-fidelity property test**
- [ ] **Step 7: Implement the single-span renderer**

```ts
export function renderMirror(task: TaskBodySpan): string {
  return task.body; // verbatim — normalization happens on read, never on write
}
```
